title: Postmortem bridgecall: reducing risk and piloting longtail mitigations
summary: Walkthrough of last week's inference degradation, discussion of root causes (KV eviction + bursty prefix patterns), agreement on a guarded pilot for caching and canary rollouts, and immediate runbook hardening actions.
action_items: Maya: Send combined postmortem deck + raw trace links to Argus team by 2026-06-12
Omar: Run targeted KV-warmup benchmark and share numbers (90th/99th p50/p95) by 2026-06-18
Ravi: Provide production traffic shape (7-day qps/sequence distribution) to Redwood by 2026-06-13
Jocelyn: Define ML acceptance criteria for hallucination / F1 regression for the pilot by 2026-06-16
Samir: Schedule pilot kickoff (week of 2026-06-22) and confirm stakeholders by 2026-06-15
next_steps: Redwood to deliver pilot plan with rollback safeguards and cost estimate
Customer to approve pilot traffic slice and success metrics
Set up a 2-week guarded pilot with canary at 5% traffic, auto-fallback to model-variant B
Weekly sync during pilot, daily standups first 3 days
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (AE), Omar (SE) - Redwood; Elena (CTO), Ravi (SRE), Jocelyn (Head ML), Samir (Prod Ops) - Argus Retail
Shared artifacts: postmortem slide deck (shared), argus-traces-20260607.zip (link), 'pilot-scope-draft.md' (shared)

[00:00] Maya: alright everyone thanks for carving time, we'll go 45-ish, open agenda is to walk through the postmortem details and lock pilot scope. Elena you want to kick off with the customer lens?

[00:18] Elena: yeah thanks Maya, we had a pretty nasty hour on Thursday — customer-facing search suggestions went from 120ms to >700ms and then we had a burst of hallucinations in the rerank responses which is, uh, really sensitive for us. That's what triggered the escalation.

[00:36] Ravi: to add, from infra it looked like there were multiple small requests with long prefixes that caused KV churn, eviction rates spiked, and then cache warmup couldn't keep up when traffic shifted. We saw retry storms too.

[00:52] Omar: right, on our side the trace shows KV cache eviction at t=14:02 correlating with a sudden drop in hit-rate. The serving runtime fell back to model-variant B for some shards, which has different prompt conditioning and caused several hallucinations — not ideal.

[01:15] Jocelyn: small clarification — when you say "model-variant B" is that the quantized fallback or a smaller architecture?

[01:22] Omar: it's a 7B quantized variant we use as a cost-safe fallback; sometimes the tokenization/temperatures are slightly different and that can change the output distribution. The fallbacks were automatic based on our capacity policy.

[01:36] Samir: the business impact was high — we had ~3% of sessions with misleading product suggestions. Not catastrophic in volume, but high risk.

[01:46] Maya: okay thanks — goal today is agreed RCA and a mitigation plan that doesn't add too much cost or latency. Let's go through timeline (slide 3 in deck).

[02:02] Maya: quick note on transcription ... some words in the auto transcripts are odd, e.g., we had 'K V' split out, sometimes 'cannery' for canary — sorry for noise.

[02:14] Omar: timeline summary: pre-incident traffic was steady; around 13:58 sequence-length tail increased (longer product queries), prefix reuse dropped, cache eviction % rose from 6% to 48% in ~3 minutes. Our LRU thresholds triggered aggressive GC.

[02:35] Ravi: question — is there a way to prevent the GC from going full-tilt? We have capacity but the pattern was pathological.

[02:44] Omar: yes we've got two levers: conservative eviction tuning for hot-prefix retention, and targeted prefetch/pinning for top prefixes (Argus top 200 queries). Prefetch would warm KV before high QPS windows.

[03:00] Jocelyn: is prefetch safe for PII-sensitive inputs? Some of our queries contain tokens we don't want stored long-term.

[03:08] Omar: good call — prefetch respects retention TTLs and can be configured to skip inputs flagged by policy. We can also use encrypted ephemeral caches for sensitive keys.

[03:20] Elena: I want to understand hallucination risk — if fallback triggers, what stops a bad output reaching production?

[03:27] Omar: we have output filters and an optional reranker that can verify top-k likelihoods, but in this incident the reranker was overloaded due to retries; that created a window where fallback outputs passed through.

[03:42] Maya: so mitigation should be multi-layer: prevent eviction, throttle retries, and harden reranker / add circuit breaker.

[03:51] Ravi: quick reality check — how invasive are these changes? We can't afford 3-day outages for the patch.

[03:57] Omar: none of the proposed changes require schema migrations or data plane downtime. Eviction tuning and pinning are runtime flags, retry throttles are config, and the reranker capacity can be increased in Dedicated pools or short-term scale-up.

[04:12] Samir: cost question — if we pin a bunch of prefixes, does that spike GPU usage?

[04:18] Omar: it increases memory pressure but we can target only top-N customer prefixes (Argus-specific) and use a guarded pilot to measure unit cost impact. We estimate 6-12% additional GPU memory for the pilot slice.

[04:32] Elena: acceptable if we can prove it reduces both latency tail and hallucination rate.

[04:38] Maya: pilot proposal (slide 7): 2-week guarded pilot, 5% traffic canary, pin top-200 prefixes + conservative eviction thresholds, add a soft circuit-breaker for the reranker so it returns cached safe outputs under overload, and auto-fallback to a warmed model-variant with identical conditioning instead of the current quantized variant.

[04:58] Jocelyn: that last part — "warmed model-variant with identical conditioning" — can you expand?

[05:04] Omar: sure. We can pre-spin a variant that's functionally equivalent (same tokenizer and temperature) with different performance knobs (e.g., larger KV cache, slightly lower batch size) so if we need to fallback it's less likely to change semantics. It costs more but avoids output drift.

[05:22] Jocelyn: ok good, that's a big plus.

[05:26] Ravi: who owns rollback if the pilot shows small regressions? We need a clear abort condition.

[05:31] Maya: abort conditions proposed: >1% increase in hallucination F1 delta or >20% p95 latency regression on the canary slice sustained for 10 minutes. We can tighten thresholds with Argus.

[05:45] Elena: can we also add a manual kill switch and an automated spike detector?

[05:49] Omar: yes both — auto spike detector will cut canary to 0% and run a notification to oncall. Manual kill switch in the console.

[06:00] Samir: what about audit logs and SSO for access during the pilot? We need RBAC to restrict who can flip flags.

[06:06] Maya: Redwood will enable restricted roles for the pilot and forward SOC2 audit snippets. I'll attach the security appendix to the deck.

[06:15] Jocelyn: on metrics — we want to track hallucination rate (human-labeled subset), model drift score, p50/p95 latency, KV hit-rate, eviction rate, and cost delta.

[06:27] Omar: agreed. We'll produce weekly dashboards and a short-lived sampling pipeline to label outputs. We also recommend adding a synthetic workload that mimics Argus long-prefix patterns for pre-pilot stress testing.

[06:41] Ravi: about that synthetic workload — do you have an example harness or script?

[06:45] Omar: yes, we have a generator (we'll share) that replays sequence lengths and prefix variety. It lives in our bench repo; I'll link after the call.

[06:55] Maya: ok let's dig into the technical detail — raw trace excerpt (Omar)

[07:00] Omar: reading wall of traces: "14:01:12 EVICT key: user:search:prefix:abc123; 14:01:12 retry x3; 14:01:13 fallback to variant-B; 14:01:18 rerank queueing 87ms -> 2.1s" — small mis-transcribed bits in the auto transcript, but that's the gist.

[07:21] Jocelyn: are KV keys deterministic? If we change hashing could that reduce collision/eviction?

[07:26] Omar: hash changes are risky in prod; we prefer caching strategy and TTL rather than keyspace reshuffle. We can do a canary with modified hashing in a separate pilot if you want to explore later.

[07:40] Samir: timeline for action — we need a tangible pilot plan by Monday. What's realistic?

[07:45] Maya: Redwood will send a compact pilot plan and cost estimates by 2026-06-12 (action), Omar will deliver the bench numbers by 6/18, Argus provides traffic shape by 6/13. Pilot kickoff week-of 6/22 as discussed.

[08:00] Elena: one more ask — can Redwood run a short A/B on the canary that includes a 'safe-output' reranker that throws out low-confidence results to reduce business risk?

[08:09] Omar: yes, the reranker thresholder can be stricter on the canary. That will reduce throughput but within the pilot budget that's acceptable.

[08:18] Jocelyn: slight tangent — Samir you mentioned token billing spikes earlier, how do we monitor cost during pilot?

[08:24] Samir: we'll need per-route token breakdowns and daily cost delta reports. Our finance team requires visibility.

[08:30] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost; we'll add a daily digest for the pilot.

[08:35] Ravi: question about observability — can we get traces correlated to customer session ids? During the incident we had partial mapping and it slowed debugging.

[08:43] Omar: yes we can include session id propagation hooks. That needs a small SDK flag change on Argus end; we can coordinate.

[08:52] Elena: security again — we need KMS integration for the ephemeral cache keys and an audit trail of who toggled pilot flags.

[08:58] Maya: noted, we'll include KMS/ HSM options in the security appendix and confirm RBAC roles.

[09:06] Samir: back to mitigation specifics — what about retry damping? We want retries to back off faster to avoid overload.

[09:13] Omar: we propose exponential backoff with jitter and an overall client-side concurrency cap. This is low-lift and effective.

[09:22] Jocelyn: in case the canary still causes regressions, what are fallbacks?

[09:27] Maya: fallback path is: auto-cut canary, revert eviction config, and serve from warmed variant with identical conditioning. If that doesn't work, immediate full rollback to pre-pilot config.

[09:37] Elena: what's the expected user-visible latency improvement if pinning reduces eviction?

[09:42] Omar: conservative estimate: p95 down from 700ms to ~220–300ms on pinning+reranker scaling; again bench numbers to follow.

[09:53] Ravi: will the KV eviction fix introduce cold-start tail for new prefixes?

[09:58] Omar: possibly, which is why we'll only pin top prefixes and leave LRU for the rest; synthetic prefetch can help cold starts.

[10:08] Maya: wrapping with a quick recap and owners (slide 12).

[10:12] Maya: Action owners: Maya send deck, Omar bench + bench script link, Ravi supply traffic shape, Jocelyn define acceptance metrics, Samir schedule pilot. Pilot kickoff week of 6/22.

[10:25] Elena: thanks all, appreciated the practical plan. The team wants a short executive note after pilot sign-off.

[10:33] Maya: we'll provide a one-pager executive summary post-pilot.

[10:37] Omar: I'll also include a small runbook snippet in the repo for oncall steps if the pilot triggers any anomalies.

[10:45] Samir: ok, any final questions?

[10:48] Jocelyn: just wonder if there's any legal / procurement touchpoint before we scale the warmed variant - internal procurement needs heads-up.

[10:55] Maya: good point — we'll loop in Redwood sales ops and legal if the pilot requires an amendment.

[11:02] Elena: thank you, we'll review the deck and expect the pilot plan Monday.

[11:07] Maya: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned. We'll follow up in writing with the attachments.

Notes on transcript quality: there are some mis-heard tokens (e.g., 'k v', 'cannery', 'quan-tization'), and timestamps are approximate.
